claim: Concept-pair link prediction on literature graphs beats chance by a wide margin (AUC 0.85 in 2020 for 5-year horizon; 0.93-0.98 in 2025 with 141 features). (all from one research group, Krenn et al.)
agent_test: Build a concept graph over our own session notes; predict which concept pairs get linked later; check AUC above 0.7 at equal tokens vs random retrieval.

claim: Link prediction is easy for strong, repeated links (AUC about 99%) and hard for single new links (up to 0.93); low-citation vs high-citation is far harder (AUC 0.67-0.7). (all from one research group, Krenn et al.)
agent_test: Report retrieval quality split by easy (repeated) vs rare links.

claim: Shared-neighbour / triadic closure (distance-2 pairs) is where most novel links appear.
agent_test: Retrieve analogues two hops from the current concept first; compare with nearest-embedding only.

claim: Literature networks grow more centralised over time (clustering 0.919 to 0.650, 1999-2013) and edges concentrate in hubs. (all from one research group, Krenn et al.)
agent_test: Warn: hub-biased retrieval over-serves popular concepts; test with degree-penalised ranking.

claim: Unsupervised embeddings of abstracts can rank untested materials; predicted items were studied later more often than random (top-10 power factor 3.6x candidate mean).
agent_test: Use embedding dot product to rank unseen analogue candidates. NOTE the '8 times' figure in a19 was not found when rechecked.

claim: Adding people (author) links to the graph raises discovery-prediction precision (up to 400%; 42% vs 10-12%).
agent_test: Not testable for a single agent; analogue: add 'source/tool used' edges to memory graph.

claim: Avoiding crowded regions (alien hypotheses) delays human discovery; surprise-based combinations get cited more (4-5x top-decile).
agent_test: Penalise candidates close to the agent's own prior outputs; measure novelty and correctness at equal tokens.

claim: Science's real strategy is conservative: 85.8% repeats vs 14.2% new; rare jump strategies earn more citations; MEDLINE strategy is far less efficient than the best alternative past 13% coverage.
agent_test: Mix exploit/explore in retrieval (e.g. 85/15) and compare with greedy.

claim: LLM ideas are rated more novel than expert human ideas (5.64 vs 4.84; rerank 5.81) but not more feasible (6.34 vs 6.61, n.s.). Update: after execution by 43 experts, LLM idea scores fell 1.0 to 1.9 points while human ideas did not move; ranking flipped (effectiveness 4.13 vs 4.78, not significant at N=43).
agent_test: Do not rank ideas by novelty rating; check each against an executable test. Same group as the original (Si et al.), NLP only; no outside replication found.

claim: LLM idea generation collapses in diversity: only about 200 of 4,000 seeds are non-duplicates (cosine 0.8).
agent_test: Measure duplicate rate vs sample count; test whether graph-neighbour seeding raises unique share.

claim: LLM self-judgement of ideas is unreliable: Claude-3.5 pairwise ranker 53.3% on idea data vs 56.1% human inter-reviewer, though 71.4% on ICLR accept/reject. Update: off-the-shelf frontier models are near chance at predicting which idea works; paper retrieval lifted one model from 38.8% to 53.0%, and fine-tuning reached 77%.
agent_test: Do not rely on self-ranking of ideas; test ranker accuracy against external outcome.

claim: Knowledge-graph neighbours added to prompts give only modest gains in human judged quality (GPT4FS+KG preferred 48-55%, mostly ties); iterative novelty boosting raises novelty in about 55% of ideas per round.
agent_test: Run iterative novelty refinement with and without graph context at equal tokens.

claim: Graph-predicted high-citation pairs were not rated more interesting by experts than random pairs (2.350 vs 2.446 of 5); mean interest 2.40; interest correlates negatively with degree and semantic distance.
agent_test: Impact prediction is not interest prediction, and review-style scores do not predict executed outcomes (weak correlation, negative for AI excitement). Do not use citation-style or review scores to pick ideas.

claim: Graph-based retrieval improves multi-hop QA over dense retrieval (HippoRAG 2Wiki R@5 89.5 vs 68.2; avg 72.9 vs 65.6) but not on HotpotQA (76.2-77.7 vs 79.3). Update: HippoRAG 2 closes the HotpotQA gap (recall@5 96.3 vs 94.5), but in a unified benchmark flat RAG wins single-hop (NQ F1 64.78 vs 61.03) and a token-matched RAG erases the overall graph edge (69.33 vs 69.01 on MultiHop-RAG); the edge remains on temporal questions (36.71 vs 50.60).
agent_test: Route by query type: flat retrieval by default, graph path for temporal or comparison multi-hop. Test at equal tokens.

claim: Community-summary graph RAG beats naive RAG on global sensemaking questions (comprehensiveness win 72-83%, LLM judge); cheapest root-level summaries weakest.
agent_test: Test on whole-corpus questions; LLM-judge bias is a caveat.

claim: Agentic linked memory cuts tokens per answer (643 vs 16,910 for MemGPT) with higher F1 on LoCoMo. Update: in the Mem0 paper itself, flat Mem0 gets J 66.88 at 1,764 tokens vs full context 72.90 at 26,031; the graph variant adds 1.56 points for twice the tokens and nothing on single- or multi-hop. Vendor-run.
agent_test: Replicate with our memory at equal token budget.

claim: LLMs beat domain experts at predicting neuroscience results (81.4% vs 63.4%); fine-tuning on 1.3B tokens adds about 3%.
agent_test: Prediction of outcomes from literature is a plausible calibration check; not a scaffold element.

claim: Graph memory is task-dependent: flat retrieval wins single-hop detail questions; graph retrieval helps temporal, comparison and complex multi-hop questions, with gains of 2-3 points overall and about 14 points on temporal questions at matched tokens.
agent_test: Build a router: flat for lookup, graph for temporal or multi-hop. Compare at equal tokens.

claim: Graph memory has a build cost: HippoRAG 2 used 9.2M input and 3.0M output tokens to index 11,656 passages (GraphRAG 115.5M, LightRAG 68.5M, plain embedding none). Query prompts range from 1.0k tokens (HippoRAG 2) to 331k (MS-GraphRAG global) against 0.9k for flat RAG.
agent_test: Count build plus query tokens; use a graph only when memory is large and long-lived.

claim: LLM-extracted entity graphs lose content: only about 65% of answer entities appear in the graph, so graph-only retrieval trails flat RAG (HotpotQA F1 25.02 vs 60.04).
agent_test: Keep raw text linked to graph nodes.

claim: LLM idea quality ratings from reviews or models do not carry through to executed outcomes; pre- and post-execution scores correlate weakly.
agent_test: Require an executable check before ranking an idea as good.
